back: Processing agricultural products (crops, livestock, timber) into food, drink, fibre and other goods.
Adding value to a raw material, especially a mineral, inside the country before export.
Making goods at home that were previously imported, to save foreign currency and create jobs.
Concentrated along the Harare–Bulawayo railway (Harare, Bulawayo, Kadoma, Kwekwe, Gweru); Mutare and the Lowveld are smaller centres.
Triangle and Hippo Valley near Chiredzi mill irrigated cane; molasses is used to make ethanol at Triangle.
Ferrochrome smelting near Kwekwe uses chrome ore from the Great Dyke; the Redcliff steelworks stopped production in the late 2000s.
Power cuts, foreign-currency shortages, obsolete machinery, competition from imports, high transport costs, emigration of skilled workers.
More power capacity and solar, credit for retooling, import duties and buy-local campaigns, railway rehabilitation, special economic zones.
Flows of goods and services between firms: backward linkages to suppliers, forward linkages to customers.
